answer: Collateralized fidelity bonds deter Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock verifiable capital in a time-locked smart contract that slashes deposits upon proven protocol equivocation. Attackers incur real opportunity cost and capital-at-risk per identity, whether deploying agents to survey a lagoon, relay summit telemetry, or filter acoustic whisper anomalies. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund multiple identities in proportion to their capital reserves.
